questions.prompt:
Which unusual article does the following describe?

This is an ancient work of prose fiction written in Greek by a satirist in the 2nd century CE. It describes a fantastical voyage in which the narrator and his companions are swept up by a storm, travel to the moon, witness a war between celestial kingdoms, and encounter many other bizarre creatures and lands. The author explicitly states at the outset that everything in the narrative is false, poking fun at other writers and historians who presented tall tales as factual accounts. Because of its depictions of space travel, alien life, and interplanetary conflict, the work is often cited by scholars as one of the earliest known examples of science fiction.
questions.hint: It is not the choice referencing a single lunar journey narrative by the same author, nor the one about a man transformed into a donkey.
questions.explanation: The article describes 'A True Story' by Lucian of Samosata, a satirical 2nd century work that parodies fantastical travel tales and includes a trip to the moon and an interplanetary war, making it a precursor to science fiction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a real, unusual conceptual artwork from the early 1960s that humorously treated a bodily product as the literal medium of the piece, satirizing the art market by packaging it as a readymade?
questions.hint: This piece was created by an Italian conceptual artist in 1961, and it has nothing to do with sound or crying, so you can rule out anything tied to breath or tears.
questions.explanation: Piero Manzoni's 1961 work consisted of 90 cans supposedly filled with his own feces, satirizing the art market by literally packaging bodily waste as a readymade.

questions.prompt: This internet meme came from a reality show audition where a contestant's heavily accented, mispronounced lyrics turned into viral nonsense phrases, inspiring remixes and parodies online. The clip's most famous garbled line, 'Tulibu dibu douchoo!', came from her attempt to sing a specific pop ballad. Which song was she actually trying to perform?
choices: Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You'
Celine Dion's 'My Heart Will Go On'
questions.hint: The song was not by Celine Dion or Adele.
questions.explanation: The meme originated from Bulgarian singer Valentina Hasan's 2007 audition on 'Music Idol', where her mispronounced rendition of Mariah Carey's 'Without You' produced viral gibberish phrases like 'Ken Lee' and 'Tulibu dibu douchoo'.

questions.prompt:
Which unusual article does the following describe?

This entry covered a niche website that compiled photos and videos of women whose vehicles had become immobilized in difficult terrain. The site developed a small but dedicated online following within a particular internet fetish community. The Wikipedia page documenting it became a notable case study in discussions about which obscure internet subcultures deserve encyclopedic coverage, and it was eventually removed for failing to meet notability standards.
choices: A forum dedicated to collecting vintage traffic camera footage
A fansite devoted to cataloguing celebrity shoe collections
A website specializing in photos of vehicles trapped in difficult terrain
A blog focused on reviewing off-road vehicle modifications
questions.hint: The correct answer is not about reviewing or modifying vehicles, and it is not about footwear.
questions.explanation: The article described Carstuckgirls.com, a niche fetish website featuring images and videos of women whose cars were stuck, which gained some notoriety in online discussions about Wikipedia's coverage of obscure topics before being deleted for lack of notability.

questions.prompt: This man was the subject of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court case that helped reinstate capital punishment in America. Years later, he broke out of death row, and that very night he died in a violent altercation in another state. In which state did this fatal incident occur?
questions.hint: It was not Georgia, where he had been held on death row, and it was not Tennessee.
questions.explanation: Troy Leon Gregg escaped from Georgia's death row in 1980, and that same night he was killed in a bar fight in North Carolina.

questions.prompt: This article describes a finite mathematical group of order exactly 17,971,200. It occupies an unusual position in classification schemes: some mathematicians treat it as part of a family of Lie type groups, while others count it as an exceptional case alongside the sporadic simple groups. It is named after the 20th century mathematician who first identified it while studying algebraic groups.
questions.hint: The correct group is not named after Zvonimir Janko, who has several sporadic groups named after him, nor after Dieter Held, whose name is attached to a different sporadic group.
questions.explanation: The Tits group, denoted ²F₄(2)', has order 17,971,200 and is named after Belgian mathematician Jacques Tits. It is unusual because it is sometimes classified as a group of Lie type and sometimes considered the 27th sporadic simple group.

questions.prompt: Before steam and diesel engines, a few boats got their push the old-fashioned way, with animals aboard supplying the muscle for paddlewheels instead of sails or an engine. Which of these is a real 19th century craft built this way?
questions.hint: It wasn't the ox-powered ferry, and it wasn't the dog-powered sled boat either.
questions.explanation: Experiment was an early 1800s boat whose paddlewheels were turned by eight horses walking on a treadmill mechanism, giving it quite literal horsepower.

questions.prompt: This long-running cigarette advertising campaign took an unusual approach by showing its customers sporting black eyes, implying they'd rather brawl than switch brands. Which advertising agency created this campaign?
questions.hint: It was not the agency famous for the Marlboro Man campaign (Leo Burnett), nor the one known for Pepsi's 'Pepsi Generation' ads (BBDO).

article.title: Us Tareyton smokers would rather fight than switch!

questions.explanation: The campaign was created by Doyle Dane Bernbach (DDB), a prominent advertising agency, and ran for many years featuring people with black eyes to suggest their loyalty to Tareyton cigarettes.

questions.prompt: This practice from a South Pacific island nation involves men leaping from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles, and it is often cited as the inspiration for a popular modern extreme sport. For the ritual to be considered successful, which part of a jumper's body is supposed to brush the ground below?
questions.hint: It's not the hands, and it's not the knees.
questions.explanation: In the Naghol ritual on Pentecost Island, Vanuatu, the vine is measured so the jumper's shoulders just touch the earth, a sign believed to ensure a good yam harvest. This practice is considered the precursor to modern bungee jumping.

questions.prompt: This Wikipedia article covers a chaotic and closely scrutinized vote-counting dispute from a U.S. presidential election, a saga so strange that it has been said it has to be read to be believed. One of its oddest details involves a minor-party candidate who received a surprisingly large number of votes in a single county, far more than anywhere else in the state, which many attributed to a confusing ballot layout. Which candidate benefited from this apparent mix-up?
questions.hint: The candidate was not one of the two major party nominees in the election.

article.title: 2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida

questions.explanation: In Palm Beach County, the confusing 'butterfly ballot' led many voters who intended to vote for Al Gore to accidentally mark Pat Buchanan, giving him an unusually high vote total there compared to the rest of Florida.
